**Naming of the surah**

• It is called al-Hujurat (The Private Chambers), because the chambers of the Prophet's house are mentioned in it, in the account of the Banu Tamim calling out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from behind his chambers.

**Among the aims of the surah**

• The training of the believers and their guidance to exalt the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger ﷺ, and that this is among the requirements of faith, and their instruction in some of the etiquette they must observe with the Prophet ﷺ in dealing with him, addressing him, and calling out to him.

• The purification of the Muslim society from the ugly morals that lead to severance and mutual hatred, such as mockery, deriding one another with nicknames, evil suspicion, spying, and backbiting (ghibah).

• An explanation of the wisdom behind the creation of people and their division into diverse peoples (shu'ub) and tribes (qaba'il), and an explanation that preference with Allah is by taqwa (God-consciousness).

• An explanation of the greatness of faith, and that it is not merely a claim a person makes, but a matter that settles in the heart, and is confirmed by speech, action, and striving (jihad) in the way of Allah, exalted is He.

**[The Tafsir]**

﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

"Do not decide a matter ahead of Allah and His Messenger, from the laws of your religion, lest you innovate (tabtadi'u), and fear Allah in your words and deeds, lest the command of Allah and His Messenger be opposed. Indeed, Allah is Hearing of your statements and Knowing of your intentions and actions." In this is a warning to the believers not to innovate in the religion, or to legislate what Allah has not permitted.

O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him as some of you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds be nullified while you do not perceive. Honour him in your address to him as he is distinguished from others by being chosen to carry the message of his Lord, and by the obligation to believe in him, to love him, to obey him and to follow his example; for fear that your deeds should be rendered void while you are unaware and do not sense it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 49, verse 3:

Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested and purified for His piety. For them is forgiveness from Allah for their sins, and a great reward, which is Paradise.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 49, verse 4:

Indeed, those who call out to you, O Prophet, from behind your private chambers with raised voices, most of them lack the intellect that would move them to observe good manners toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to honor him.

If they had shown patience until you came out to them, it would have been better for them in the sight of Allah. For Allah has commanded them to show you honor and respect. And Allah is Oft-Forgiving toward what proceeded from them out of ignorance, of sins and of breaches of etiquette, and Most Merciful toward them in that He did not hasten to punish them.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law: if a deviator (fasiq) comes to you with news, then verify it before accepting it as true and passing it on, until you know that it is sound; lest you harm a people in ignorance, through a wrong you have committed against them, and then come to regret what you have done.

Know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. So show him proper manners, for he knows better than you what is good for you, and he wishes you well. You may wish for yourselves some evil and harm that the Messenger would not agree with; if he were to obey you in many matters that you choose, that would lead to your hardship. But Allah made faith beloved to you and beautified it in your hearts, so you believed, and He made disbelief in Allah and departure from His obedience, and disobedience to Him, hateful to you. Those who are characterized by these qualities are the rightly guided, who follow the path of truth.

This blessing that they received is a favor from Allah upon them and a grace. And Allah is All-Knowing of those who are grateful for His blessings, All-Wise in the management of the affairs of His creation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 49, verse 9:

And if two groups of the believers fight each other, then make peace between them, O believers, by calling them to refer their dispute to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), and to accept their judgment. But if one of the two groups transgresses and refuses to accept this, then fight against it until it returns to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger. If it returns, then make peace between them with equity, and act justly in your judgment, by not going beyond the judgment of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger in your rulings. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly in their judgments, who judge among His creation with fairness. In the verse is the affirmation of the attribute of love for Allah in its true sense, as befits His majesty, glory be to Him.
﴿Indeed, the believers are but brothers in faith, so make peace between your two brothers when they fight, and fear Allah in all your affairs, that you may receive mercy.﴾

O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps the latter may be better than the former. Nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps the latter may be better than the former. And do not defame one another, nor call one another by offensive nicknames. How wicked is the name of defiance after faith! And whoever does not repent, it is they who are the wrongdoers.

This is a translation of the commentary text, which is itself a paraphrase (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) of the verse. The Qur'anic quotation is marked with ﴿ ﴾, and the passage is rendered as it stands.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 49, verse 12:**

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and act according to His law, avoid much of suspicion about the believers; indeed, some suspicion is sinful. Do not spy on the private faults of the Muslims, and do not speak of one another in his absence with what he would dislike. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You certainly hate that, so hate backbiting (ghibah). And fear Allah in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you. Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance from His servants who are believers, and Merciful to them.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsīr al-Muyassar, a simplified Qur'anic exegesis) on Surah 49, verse 13:**

﴿O mankind, indeed We created you from one father, Adam, and one mother, Hawwa' (Eve). So there should be no boasting among you on account of lineage. We made you into peoples and tribes through procreation, so that you may come to know one another. Indeed, the most honoured of you in the sight of Allah is the one most mindful of Him. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of the God-fearing, and All-Aware of them.﴾

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 49, verse 14:

The Bedouins said: "We believe in Allah and His Messenger with complete faith." Say to them, O Prophet: "Do not claim for yourselves complete faith, but say: 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not diminish for you anything from the reward of your deeds. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving to whoever repents of his sins, Most Merciful to him."

In the verse is a warning to those who display faith and follow the Sunnah while their deeds bear witness to the contrary.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 49, verse 15:

Indeed, the believers are those who have affirmed belief in Allah and His Messenger, acted in accordance with His law, then did not doubt in their faith, and expended the precious parts of their wealth and their lives in jihad in the way of Allah, seeking His obedience and His pleasure. Those are the truthful in their faith.

Say, O Prophet, to these Bedouins: "Will you inform Allah about your religion, and about what is in your hearts, while Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? And Allah is All-Knowing of everything. Nothing is hidden from Him of what is in your hearts, whether faith or disbelief, and righteousness or wickedness."

They think they have done you a favour, O Prophet, by embracing Islam, by following you and by supporting you. Say to them: "Do not count your Islam as a favour to me. Rather, its benefit returns to you. And God has bestowed a favour upon you in that He guided you to faith in Him and in His Messenger, if you are truthful in your faith."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 49, verse 18:

Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth; nothing of that is hidden from Him. Allah is All-Seeing of your deeds, and He will recompense you for them: if it is good, (the recompense is) good, and if it is evil, (the recompense is) evil.
